unresolved.finding: The greedy wildcard after a parameter's initial value consumes the comment, unit, and description, so those named metadata groups resolve empty even for populated declarations.
The parameter-unit character class excludes slash and question-mark characters that are used by units in params.def, independently making the declared unit grammar inconsistent with its input.

The parser accepts logical, float, and complex source types and maps them to ISO types, but generation performs no capability check that the selected templates can represent those types in their introspection dispatch.

Parsed declarations are accepted without checking required JSON keys, name uniqueness, or agreement between declaration rank and JSON shape rank, allowing inconsistent definition data to fail later or generate contradictory Fortran.
Unrestricted dictionary update lets arbitrary JSON metadata overwrite parsed structural fields such as name, type, dimension, or rank.
Default template discovery deliberately relies on the undocumented glob.glob1 API.
Command-line template paths are reduced to basenames without validation, so the supplied directory is silently ignored and a same-named template from the fixed template directory is used.
Each destination is opened with truncating mode before template rendering, so a render exception can destroy the last valid generated include and leave a partial file.
Output naming replaces every occurrence of '.mako' rather than requiring it as a suffix, permitting surprising output names for malformed CLI inputs.
The generated provenance header misspells xbeachlibrary as xbeachlibray.
The parsing rules require all-lowercase declarations, but the file contains many mixed-case parameter names, leaving external script-reader compatibility dependent on undocumented tolerance.
The adjacency rule refers to nglobalvars, while the declared count parameter is nglobalvar.
Both nz and kmax are described as controlling vertical/Q3D layer counts, without explaining which count is authoritative for Q3D allocations.
dtset is a fixed timestep but is labeled dimensionless rather than in seconds.
order is declared double precision even though its description defines a discrete first-order versus second-order switch.
fwcutoff is described as a depth threshold but is labeled dimensionless.
Several declarations use nonstandard legacy spellings integer*4 and real*8 instead of portable kind-based types.
The molecular viscosity vicmol and estimated ripple height deltar are both labeled dimensionless despite requiring viscosity and length units respectively.
dispc retains a literal unknown-unit marker [?] in the source-of-truth declaration.
The integer parameters sus and bed are described as calibration factors, obscuring that their declared type permits only discrete values.
sedfricfac is described as a wave shape model even though its name and paired string parameter identify a sediment-friction selection.
bermslopedepth is described as a water depth but is labeled dimensionless.
Several parameters explicitly described as file names are labeled dimensionless instead of with the file unit marker used elsewhere.
The three pointer components have no default NULL initialization, leaving newly created parameter objects with undefined association status until an allocation path is completed.
Runup depths and station identifiers use fixed capacities of 9999 while their user-controlled counts have no local bound contract.
The file explicitly acknowledges that the projection string capacity is too short for WKT, so valid projection metadata can be truncated.
The veguntow description is visibly truncated at 'vegetati'.
cf_transport is named and typed as a dimensionless coefficient but is described as bed shear stress.
max_dzsdt is described as a maximum bed-level change rate but is labeled dimensionless.
The y-coordinate origin yzg11 is assigned the x-coordinate standard name projection_x_coordinate.
thetamaх is described as the minimum wave-grid angle even though its name and pairing with thetamin identify it as the maximum.
windlen is described as the length of the tide time series rather than the wind time series.
The spatial water-surface gradients dzsdx and dzsdy are labeled m/s, although a level derivative with respect to distance is dimensionless.
qy is described as a y-component discharge at u-points, inconsistent with the adjacent staggered-grid u/v naming.
vev is described as the Eulerian y-velocity at u-points even though its paired name indicates the v-point field.
The y-component sediment advection velocity ve_sed is assigned the x-velocity standard name sea_water_x_velocity.
dU and dV are explicitly described as velocity differences but carry acceleration-like units m2/s2 instead of m/s.
D50top and D90top are both labeled dimensionless friction coefficients, which conflicts with their grain-size names and the meter units used for D50 and D90 elsewhere in the same file.
tdisch is described as the discharge time series but is marked dimensionless rather than with time units.
The Q3D velocity fields uz, vz, and ustz and turbulence-viscosity field nutz are all labeled dimensionless despite their physical descriptions.
The header names variable.f90 rather than the parameter-definition input that actually drives the emitted key tables.
Parameter classification silently ignores every type other than the three hard-coded spellings and provides no error for an unsupported or misspelled type.

Array-valued parameters are excluded through manually maintained name lists instead of a rank/shape property, so adding or renaming an array can silently omit it or generate an invalid scalar assignment.
The header tells maintainers to edit variables.f90 instead of identifying the variables definition file that supplies the generated cases.

The header identifies spaceparams.tmpl and makeincludes.F90 as edit/build inputs, which is inconsistent with this Mako template's variables-driven interface and leaves the actual source of truth unclear.
The header names variable.f90 as the editable source although the template consumes generated variable metadata.
The type-to-code mapping is a closed three-entry dictionary with direct lookup, so any definition using an otherwise valid new type causes generation to fail with no validation-oriented diagnostic.

Definition strings are interpolated directly inside single-quoted Fortran literals without escaping embedded apostrophes, making a legitimate metadata value capable of producing malformed generated source.
The header names variable.f90 as the edit point instead of clearly identifying the generator's variable-definition source.
Indexed allocation is unconditional and has no ASSOCIATED guard or STAT handling, so allocating an already associated component can fail at runtime without a recoverable status.
No cases are emitted for scalar indices, leaving the behavior of the nominal allocate-by-index API inconsistent across entries in the shared index space.
The header points to variable.f90 as the editable source rather than clearly naming the definitions consumed by generation.
An operation named allocated reports pointer association instead, which also returns true for association with a non-owned target and has no emitted case for scalar indices.
The generated-file header directs edits to variable.f90 rather than clearly identifying the definition input used by the generator.

The indexed deallocator performs an unconditional DEALLOCATE with no ASSOCIATED check or STAT result, so a repeated call or an index whose component was never allocated can raise a Fortran runtime error.
The header identifies variable.f90 as the edit point instead of clearly naming the definition data that drives generation.
Reallocation destroys the existing target before attempting an unchecked allocation, so allocation failure loses the prior data and is not surfaced through STAT.

The code treats ASSOCIATED as proof that the pointer owns a deallocatable target, although an associated pointer can legally reference a target it does not own unless that ownership invariant is enforced elsewhere.
A case is emitted for every variable index but scalar cases contain no operation, so requesting reallocation of a scalar silently succeeds as a no-op.
The header points maintainers to variable.f90 rather than clearly identifying the variables definition input that supplies this template.
All array components are allocated unconditionally and without STAT handling, leaving repeated calls or invalid/nonpositive generated extents dependent on an undocumented caller precondition.
The branch is documented as rank-1-only but actually emits allocations for every positive rank.
The header names variable.f90 as the editable source even though component allocation is generated from the variables definition input.
All positive-rank components are unconditionally allocated as zero-size arrays without guarding against an already allocated component or reporting allocation failure.
The comment says the branch is only for rank-1 variables, while the actual condition includes every rank greater than zero.
The generated-file header directs maintainers to edit variable.f90 even though this template is driven by the variables definition input, making the stated source-of-truth contract ambiguous.

Every scalar component is allocated unconditionally without an allocated/associated guard or STAT handling, so a repeated allocation call can terminate at runtime unless an unstated fresh-object precondition always holds.

When toall is true the template selects xomaster as the source via iamsrc and xmpi_imaster, but then unconditionally returns on xomaster before any generated distribution body can use that selected source.
